name: Carbon Robotics: AI weeders, Carbon AI and farm autonomy on carbonrobotics.com
title: Carbon Robotics: AI weeders, Carbon AI and farm autonomy on carbonrobotics.com
answer: Carbon Robotics' website presents the company's physical AI for agriculture, chiefly the LaserWeeder G2 and Carbon Autonomy. Its most useful disclosure is Carbon AI, a Large Plant Model trained on 150 million labeled plants gathered by LaserWeeders in 15 countries. Operators can create Plant Profiles by selecting two or three field photos, letting the model target specific crops and weeds in real time, with improvements deployed automatically to machines in the field. The site also reports customer claims on yield, chemical reduction and labor savings.

sections.body: Carbon Robotics publishes this website. The company was founded in 2018 and is headquartered in Seattle, Washington. The pages read include product descriptions for LaserWeeder G2 and Carbon Autonomy, a Carbon AI page, a company page, a partners page and a news index. The site covers physical AI for agriculture, including weed control and tractor autonomy. The pages were read on 1 October 2026. No single publication date is stated for the site as a whole, though news headlines refer to 2023, 2025 and 2026 awards and funding.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Carbon Robotics describes Carbon AI as a system powered by a Large Plant Model trained on what it calls the world's largest, most diverse and fastest growing agricultural dataset. LaserWeeders collect labeled plant and weed data from real fields in 15 countries and continuously feed it back to strengthen the model. Model improvements are deployed automatically to all LaserWeeders in the field. Plant Profiles let the Large Plant Model be tailored to unique fields in real time. Operators select two or three photos of their field to define crop and weed conditions, and Carbon AI adjusts model behavior with no waiting or downtime. Customer quotes describe using eight plant profiles across 13 crops, tailoring the model in Vidalia onion seed beds, transplants and direct seeded onions, and adding a few images in Scotland so improvements took effect in minutes. The site says actionable visualized data includes coverage maps, weed analytics and performance metrics. Real time remote insights into LaserWeeder status, location and performance are available on iOS and Android in nine languages. A purpose built iPad app gives operators control, from a single tap to start to deep customization of weeding parameters. Carbon Autonomy uses Carbon AI for row alignment and re entry after end of row turnarounds. The company also describes LaserWeeder G2 and Carbon Autonomy, with autonomy kits installed on certain Deere tractors and remote operators supervising in real time.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that Carbon Robotics was founded in 2018, is headquartered in Seattle, Washington, generates over $100M in annual revenue and is trusted by top growers in 15 countries. It says the Large Plant Model is trained on 150 million labeled plants. It says Plant Profiles require operators to select two or three photos. A customer quote says the farm grows 13 different crops and uses eight plant profiles. The site says remote insights are available in nine languages. It says payback is in one to three years on equipment built to last a decade. It says Carbon Autonomy Kits fit Deere 6R, 8R, 8RX and 8RT tractors from 2019 onward with no permanent modifications. Customer quotes claim about a 20 to 30 percent yield improvement, a 70 percent reduction in chemical use, weeding labor reduced by over 50 percent, and costs falling from over $1 million to maybe $100,000 to $200,000 at most. News headlines list funding rounds of $70 million Series D, $20 million, $30 million, $27 million Series B and an additional $8 million, a LaserWeeder with 30 lasers, and a Western Growers report headline saying 70 percent of specialty crop growers are investing in farm robots. Partner descriptions include iMerit labeling plant imagery for Carbon AI, Starlink connecting machines across 15 countries, and Great Plains as the first Carbon Autonomy Ready member.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in agriculture, this source is useful because it describes a commercial large plant model and the data pipeline behind it, not just a concept. It shows how field data from machines in 15 countries is labeled, fed back and deployed automatically, and how operators can tailor a model to a specific field with a few photos. It also shows how computer vision and lasers are packaged as farm equipment, with remote supervision and tractor autonomy kits. The customer claims on yield, chemical reduction and labor savings give a vendor's view of the operational case, while the partner list shows the ecosystem needed for connectivity, annotation, manufacturing and financing.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Agriculture

sections.body: This is a commercial vendor website, so its claims are promotional and not independently verified. It does not provide methodology for the yield, chemical reduction, labor or cost figures, and it does not discuss failures, limitations or competing systems. The news page is an index of headlines rather than full articles. The site gives no pricing, no detailed technical architecture and no peer reviewed results. Many pages carry no publication date, and the customer quotes are testimonials. The scope is Carbon Robotics' own products, LaserWeeder G2 and Carbon Autonomy, so it is partial rather than a survey of AI in agriculture.
